scope_of_spec: POST /check route handler: request validation, outbound HTTP GET with high-resolution timing, error handling, and delegation to the Database Layer for persistence.
overview: The Check Handler owns the POST /check endpoint. It validates that the request body contains a well-formed URL, measures wall-clock elapsed time using process.hrtime.bigint(), performs an outbound HTTP GET to the target URL using the built-in Node.js fetch API, persists the result to the Database Layer (C-4), and returns a JSON response. On network failure or timeout the handler persists a failure record and returns a descriptive response rather than crashing. It exports an Express Router that is mounted by C-1.
responsibilities: Validate that req.body.url is present and is a valid absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.
Record a high-resolution start time using process.hrtime.bigint() immediately before the outbound request.
Perform an outbound HTTP GET to the target URL using the Node.js global fetch() with a configurable timeout (default: 10 000 ms).
Calculate elapsed time in milliseconds from the bigint delta: Number(end - start) / 1_000_000, rounded to one decimal place.
On successful response: extract the HTTP status code.
On network error or timeout: record status_code as null and capture the error message string.
Call C-4 insertCheck({ url, status_code, response_time_ms, error }) synchronously.
Return HTTP 200 with { id, url, status_code, response_time_ms, error, checked_at } on both success and handled failure.
Return HTTP 400 with { error: '<message>' } when URL validation fails.
Export the handler as an Express Router.

apis.name: POST /check
apis.description: Accepts a JSON body with a url field, performs an HTTP GET to that URL, persists the result, and returns the check record.

request.body_schema: { url: string } — url must be a non-empty string parseable by the URL constructor with protocol http: or https:

response.body_schema: 200: { id: number, url: string, status_code: number | null, response_time_ms: number, error: string | null, checked_at: string (ISO-8601) } | 400: { error: string }

fields.url: string — the URL that was checked
fields.status_code: number | null — HTTP status code returned by target, or null on network error
fields.response_time_ms: number — wall-clock ms from request start to first response byte (or error), 1 decimal place
fields.error: string | null — error message when fetch fails, otherwise null
fields.checked_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC timestamp set by the Database Layer at insert time

behavior: If req.body.url is absent or not a string, respond HTTP 400 { error: 'url is required and must be a string' }.
Attempt to construct new URL(req.body.url). If it throws, respond HTTP 400 { error: 'Invalid URL: <message>' }.
If the parsed URL protocol is not 'http:' or 'https:', respond HTTP 400 { error: 'URL must use http or https protocol' }.
On AbortError or other fetch error: statusCode = null, errorMsg = err.message.
Record endNs = process.hrtime.bigint(); responseTimeMs = round(Number(endNs - startNs) / 1_000_000, 1 decimal).
Call insertCheck({ url, status_code: statusCode, response_time_ms: responseTimeMs, error: errorMsg ?? null }).
Respond HTTP 200 with the full inserted record returned by insertCheck (including id and checked_at).
edge_cases: Target URL times out (no response within 10 000 ms): AbortSignal.timeout() causes fetch to throw an AbortError. The handler must catch this, record status_code=null and error='TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout' (or equivalent), persist, and return HTTP 200 with the failure record.

Target URL returns a 5xx status code (e.g., 503): This is a valid HTTP response — the handler must record the actual status code (503) and treat it as a success from the perspective of the check. No error is recorded.
req.body is missing entirely (Content-Type not set, or empty body): express.json() will set req.body to undefined or {}. The validator must treat a missing url field as a 400 error.

Target URL redirects (e.g., HTTP 301 → 302 → 200): Node.js fetch follows redirects by default (up to 20). The final status code after following all redirects is recorded. Response time covers the full redirect chain.
Target URL has a non-HTTP protocol (e.g., ftp://...): URL constructor succeeds but protocol check fails — return HTTP 400.
constraints_and_considerations: Must use process.hrtime.bigint() for timing — not Date.now() — to avoid wall-clock skew (NFR-1).
Fetch timeout is implemented via AbortSignal.timeout(10_000). This value is a resolved design decision; default is 10 000 ms.
Node.js built-in fetch (available since Node 18) is used. No additional HTTP client library is required, keeping dependencies minimal (intent: simplicity weight=9).
The handler must never throw an unhandled exception to Express. All fetch errors must be caught within the handler.
C-4 insertCheck is synchronous (better-sqlite3); no async coordination needed after fetch resolves.
The handler exports an Express Router — it does not call app.listen() or reference the app instance.
Design decision (resolved): Follow HTTP redirects by default (Node.js fetch default behavior). Justification: simulates real browser behavior; most health checks expect the resolved destination.
Design decision (resolved): Timeout default is 10 000 ms. Justification: reasonable for health checks; avoids hanging indefinitely on unresponsive hosts.
